According to recent reports, la Lazio di Gattuso ha raccolto nelle prime dodici giornate più punti di quella del 2000, considerata tra le più forti della storia biancoceleste per l’organico al completo. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Da quando la vittoria vale tre punti, soltanto la Juventus, prima con Capello e poi con Allegri, ha fatto meglio. È da questi numeri che Il Messaggero parte per accostare le due squadre, pur tenendo distinte le rispettive epoche.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Rino, Frattesi e gli altri biancocelesti continuano a guardare al traguardo dei 40 punti, indicato come quota della salvezza matematica. Dopo la vittoria sul Lecce, il tecnico calabrese aveva spiegato: «E dopo parleremo di altro, con maggiore tranquillità».

Industry observers note that il confronto con la squadra del secondo scudetto riguarda anche lo spogliatoio. Gattuso vi ha portato un clima che richiama, con le dovute proporzioni, quello creato da Eriksson ventisei anni fa. Nella Lazio di allora, però, l’armonia non era quella di oggi: convivevano il gruppo degli ex Samp, guidato da Roberto Mancini, e quello degli argentini, senza un capo designato ma rappresentato dalle personalità di Veron e Simeone.

It has been revealed that il paragone suggerito dalla partita contro il Lecce è quello tra Belahyane e Almeyda. Il marocchino intercetta palloni e li sottrae agli avversari commettendo raramente fallo, come faceva l’argentino. Almeyda era chiamato Capitan Uncino per il modo in cui usava il piede destro per portare via il pallone; Belahyane si affida invece alla rapidità della corsa e all’appoggio del corpo sul rivale per interrompere l’azione.

Tra i portieri, Mandas richiama Luca Marchegiani: entrambi efficaci tra i pali, dotati di personalità sulle palle alte e meno talentuosi nel gioco con i piedi. A Marchegiani costò il posto in Nazionale un errore che Sacchi non gli perdonò.

A centrocampo, Frattesi ricorda Nedved quando arriva nei pressi dell’area pronto a colpire. Il ceco era un attaccante aggiunto per Zoff ed Eriksson; Davide è l’incursore della squadra di Gattuso. Alcuni movimenti di Taylor richiamano Stankovic, più potente soprattutto nel tiro dalla distanza. L’olandese viene accostato anche a Simeone per la capacità di contribuire con gol e assist senza dare nell’occhio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So much for Xabi Alonso’s call for cool heads from his Chelsea players. Cole Palmer lost his and was sent off, while goalkeeper Mike Penders punched the ball into his own net to give Tottenham Hotspur a helping hand on their way to a second win at Stamford Bridge in 42 attempts.

This was hardly “the Battle of the Bridge”, but Chelsea blew up during a ridiculous 10-minute spell towards the end of a game in which Tottenham had bossed possession but not looked like scoring.

Palmer was lucky to stay on the pitch in the 70th minute, when he shoved his pelvis into the face of Mateus Fernandes after the Tottenham midfielder had stopped him racing through with a foul and a handball.

Christopher Kavanagh, the referee, let him off with a yellow card, but 10 minutes later Palmer inexplicably gave Kavanagh no choice but to book him again and send him off, following a late challenge on substitute Conor Gallagher.

Alonso had noted he was confident his players could keep calm ahead of the game, but he got that wrong – along with his team selection and substitutions.

It has been revealed that in between Palmer’s two bookings, Penders suffered his own moment of madness with a bizarre own goal on his league debut for Chelsea. The Belgian was standing in for Emi Martinez, who watched in disbelief from the home dug-out after undergoing surgery on his jaw.

It has been revealed that attimi concitati nel finale di gara tra Atalanta e Inter, con grandi proteste tra le file degli ospiti per il rigore assegnato alla Dea che poi ha portato al 4-4 finale. Ecco il racconto di quegli attimi da BordoCAM di DAZN.

Industry observers note that gattuso paragona il gesto a una giocata di Rui Costa. Per l’olandese, due gol e due assist nelle prime 12 partite.

In a recent development, il tacco di Kenneth Taylor è stato decisivo per il secondo gol di Noslin contro il Lecce. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Nella stessa gara, l’olandese ha stabilito il record di 23 palloni giocati in avanti e riusciti. Gattuso ha accostato la giocata a quelle dei campioni rossoneri con cui ha condiviso il campo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Parlando del gesto di Taylor, Gattuso ha detto: «Mi ha ricordato Rui Costa.» Poi ha aggiunto: «Anche Taylor vede cose che gli altri non vedono». Il colpo di tacco dell’olandese ha contribuito alla seconda rete di Noslin contro il Lecce.

Taylor è più continuo e completo di Luis Alberto. A Roma il centrocampista è cresciuto e, contro Cagliari, Napoli e Lecce, ha offerto tre prove caratterizzate da recuperi, accelerazioni, ripartenze e giocate di qualità. Il quotidiano lo descrive come il giocatore che cuce la manovra della squadra di Gattuso.

Il suo percorso comprende il gol decisivo segnato a Parma, seguito da una rete e un assist contro il Sassuolo. Il bilancio è di due gol, due assist e un rigore decisivo procurato a Venezia: cinque reti a cui ha contribuito in 12 partite. Nella scorsa stagione aveva raggiunto lo stesso bottino in 17 gare, dopo essere arrivato a gennaio.

It has been revealed that alle giocate decisive si sono aggiunte prestazioni senza pause. Il quotidiano presenta Taylor come un leader della Lazio. Gattuso, che durante il ritiro lo aveva rimproverato duramente nel corso di un allenamento, ora lo protegge e ne esalta il rendimento.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

L'Aston Villa potrebbe avere una nuova opportunità per riportare a casa Jack Grealish. L'esterno del Manchester City, attualmente in prestito all'Everton per la seconda stagione consecutiva, avrebbe infatti intenzione di rimanere in Premier League anche qualora non si concretizzasse il trasferimento a titolo definitivo ai Toffees. Un'eventualità che potrebbe riaprire la porta al suo ex club, soprattutto considerando che il contratto con il City scadrà la prossima estate.

Secondo quanto riportato da Football Insider, il 31enne preferirebbe continuare a giocare nel campionato inglese, nonostante l'interesse di alcune società straniere. La sua posizione rappresenta un motivo di interesse per l'Aston Villa, squadra nella quale è cresciuto e di cui è stato anche capitano prima del trasferimento al Manchester City nell'estate del 2021 per 100 milioni di sterline.

Un eventuale ritorno a Villa Park avrebbe un significato particolare per Grealish, ma il suo ruolo sarebbe diverso rispetto al passato. Il club non avrebbe più bisogno di costruire l'intero reparto offensivo attorno a lui: l'inglese dovrebbe inserirsi in una squadra che punta a competere a livelli più alti rispetto a quelli del periodo precedente alla sua partenza.

Dal punto di vista tecnico, potrebbe comunque offrire esperienza, capacità di saltare l'uomo, portare palla e mettere in difficoltà le difese avversarie. Inoltre, il suo eventuale arrivo a parametro zero rappresenterebbe un'opportunità sul piano del costo del cartellino, anche se resterebbe da trovare un accordo sullo stipendio.

Industry observers note that L'Everton ha ancora tempo per ricucire il rapporto e convincerlo a restare. Se la trattativa per il trasferimento definitivo dovesse saltare, però, l'Aston Villa potrebbe valutare concretamente il ritorno del suo ex capitano.

Aberdeen  boss Mario Frick has vowed to go on the attack when his upcoming-look team take on Rangers at Ibrox tomorrow night.

Appointed as the club's new manager during the international break, Frick's reign got off to a flyer as Aberdeen won 4-2 away at Kilmarnock on Saturday.

Renowned for a high-octane attacking style of play at his previous clubs, the 52-year-old Liechtensteiner has already generated a wave of positivity at Pittodrie.

Aberdeen will face a tough task against an in-form Rangers side who are unbeaten in their last 13 matches.

But Frick insists there is no prospect of his team turning up at Ibrox and parking the bus in their efforts to take a positive result.

'I'm looking forward to it and I'm pretty confident in our squad,' he stated. 'Now we have to prove that and have another good performance.

'That's not our style (to sit in and defend). We want to play like we did at Kilmarnock. That's our style of play.

Frick is all smiles after his side put four goals past Kilmarnock in his first match in charge.

Recent findings suggest that 'Rangers will be a tough game. They are very strong, especially at home. I saw a lot of quality, particularly in their forward areas.

'We have to defend better than we did on Saturday, that's for sure, and that's what we're working on.

'I have to get to know my players even better because it's only been a week since we arrived in Aberdeen, and that takes time.

It has been revealed that 'But, of course, it helps when you win the first game. We've got some confidence now and I'm pretty confident we can take something from Ibrox.

According to recent reports, 'At the weekend, you could see that the mentality is very good. We struggled during the first 20 minutes of the second half, but the substitutes were very good and had a huge impact.

'I think, in the end, it was a deserved win and now we're looking forward to meeting Rangers at Ibrox.

'Defensively, we have to improve. Otherwise, it will be very difficult. I'm pretty sure we can defend better.

'But, like I say, we want to play like we did at the weekend. It's not our style (just to sit back and defend).'.

Kevin Nisbet is mobbed by team-mates after netting the first of his double at Rugby Park.

After the doom and gloom of the Stephen Robinson era, Frick has immediately created a feelgood factor at Aberdeen.

The fans were singing his name after the victory at Rugby Park on Saturday - and he wants to strengthen that feeling of unity throughout the club.

'It's been very good so far, especially with the win,' he added. 'The team has some confidence now and I see many players laughing.

'That's very key because we do this for fun as well. When you go onto the pitch, you have to take things seriously, but always with enjoyment. That's very important.

'The relationship between the team and the supporters is crucial, not between the supporters and me, because the team is the most important thing.

'For the players' confidence, it was very notable that so many supporters travelled to Kilmarnock and celebrated the win with us. That was the first step.

Sources indicate that 'It's not the time for me to make a statement. It's the first time we're playing together at Ibrox, and it's important that we stick to our style of play.

'That's the most important thing to me. It is an exciting game and we are looking forward to it.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

Anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an important afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

But Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola stated. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

And how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

According to recent reports, with the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP.

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

According to recent reports, “I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two big chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an notable moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR.

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite quickly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

It has been revealed that alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb.

In a recent development, “The performance was really good,” said Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”.

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

Industry observers note that they remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

"The performance was really solid" Alexander Isak reacts after scoring in Liverpool's win against Brighton 🗣️ https://t.co/Zei2tmWVix.

Sources indicate that iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Three points at Anfield 😍 #LIVBHA https://t.co/AnAlNgOzlu.

Still, Brighton can’t find a way through Liverpool’s resilient defence. Araujo’s well-time sliding challenge on Kostoulas draws huge cheers from the home fans.

Ronald Araujo has become a cult figure very quickly and he’s just provided the moment of the second half with a challenge that was a well received by those in the Main Stand as a goal. Liverpool are working relentlessly to preserve their clean sheet and Andoni Iraola is imploring his players to retain their focus until the end.

According to recent reports, there will be four minutes of added time. Brighton need a goal as soon as possible. Liverpool are closing in on an impressive win.

So wasteful from Brighton... They have a great chance to put the ball into the box with a free kick, but De Cuyper wastefully debuts it out of play. With Gross also stood over it, you expected him take it. Liverpool then make a late change as Tsimikas replaces Kerkez for the final few minutes.

Gakpo drives forward and smashes a wild long-range shot wide. His end-product has been lacking today, but he’s undoubtedly caused Brighton problems with his dribbling, movement and directness.

In a recent development, gakpo brilliantly turns Costinha, who pulls the winger back to deservedly pick up a booking. Both sides look to be readying changes, with Ngumoha, Koumas and Rutter poised to enter the action.

Brighton seem to have hit a wall in this second half. They’ve struggled to create chances since the break. Liverpool are working really hard defensively.

This game is still very much in the balance, even though Liverpool have a two goal advantage, and it speaks volumes about both teams’ commitment to attack. The questions the respective head coaches are asking of their players are relentless but the players are responding by being adventurous in how they attack and where they want to get on the ball. How Andoni Iraola and Fabian Hurzeler deploy their substitutes will be significant.

Wirtz’s wickedly deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s neat finish from close range mean Liverpool are two goals in front against Brighton. In a recent development, C'è un dirigente in Brasile che è stato accostato ad alcuni club italiani e che recentemente ha vinto ancora. José Boto ha festeggiato con il Flamengo il Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A e ha arricchito ulteriormente il suo palmares, diventando così ancora più ambito anche in Europa. Già il Milan di Gerry Cardinale, prima di virare su Markus Krosche, ci aveva pensato la scorsa estate.

Boto è stato capace di vincere 5 volte la Liga Portugal con il Benfica, 3 volte il titolo nazionale con lo Shakhtar Donetsk e 2 quello brasiliano con il Flamengo, per un totale di 10 successi. Ciò che rende la sua impresa ancora più grande è essere riuscito a farlo con 7 allenatori diversi: Jorge Jesus e Rui Vitoria in Portogallo, Paulo Fonseca, Luis Castro e Roberto De Zerbi in Ucraina e Filipe Luis e Leonardo Jardim al Mengao. A questi vanno aggiunti anche 1 Copa Libertadores, 1 Supercoppa Brasiliana, 2 Coppe di Portogallo, 6 Coppe di Lega Portoghese, 1 Coppa di Ucraina e 1 Supercoppa Ucraina.

Boto ormai ha un curriculum di tutto rispetto, si è affermato nel tempo e la testimonianza sono le 22 coppe che ha sollevato in carriera, ma anche quelle sfiorate, come il Mondiale per Club o le due Europa League, tornei persi in finale. Nonostante sia già in una massive, potrebbe tornare nel nostro continente e cimentarsi in un'esperienza in una società che milita in uno dei principali campionati d'Europa. I sondaggi non mancano, le offerte arriveranno presto: chissà che non possa lavorare proprio in Italia, dove le proprietà puntano sempre di più su direttori sportivi stranieri.

L’ex direttore sportivo spera che il cammino biancoceleste duri tutto l’anno e vede i giallorossi in corsa fino alla fine.

Sources indicate that walter Sabatini non si aspettava di trovare Lazio e Roma ai primi due posti in campionato. L’ex direttore sportivo di entrambi i club elogia il lavoro di Gattuso con i biancocelesti e le qualità della squadra di Gasperini. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, Nella corsa allo scudetto, però, indica ancora l’Inter come favorita.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sabatini, 71 anni, racconta anche delle proprie condizioni di salute dopo gli effetti delle migliaia di sigarette fumate: «Se senti un soffietto è perché ogni tanto mi attacco all’ossigeno, ma non ne avrei neanche bisogno».

Alla domanda se avesse previsto le due squadre romane in testa, Sabatini risponde parlando prima della Roma e poi della Lazio. Attribuisce a Gattuso un lavoro sbalorditivo nella preparazione emotiva dei biancocelesti: «No. Era chiaro come la Roma fosse una squadra meravigliosa, destinata a vincere ogni partita per la determinazione, l’autorevolezza, la convinzione che la rendono quasi imbattibile. Alla Lazio ha fatto un lavoro sbalorditivo Gattuso, che ha preparato emotivamente i suoi e giocatori l’anno scorso ai margini sono diventati protagonisti».

Tra i giocatori cresciuti si sofferma soprattutto su Isaksen, dopo aver citato Belahyane e Noslin: «Penso a Belahyane, oggi invidiabile regista di copertura; a Noslin, attaccante che potrebbe giocare in qualsiasi club; a Isaksen soprattutto. Il danese ha sempre scontato una timidezza tecnica insopportabile. Le sue grandissime potenzialità le teneva nel cassetto, non prendeva rischi, adesso gioca in maniera prepotente, persino arrogante, può trasformare in oro qualsiasi situazione di gioco e questo è merito di Gattuso che ha lavorato sulla testa dei giocatori».

Recent findings suggest that per Sabatini sarebbe riduttivo identificare Gattuso soltanto con la grinta. All’allenatore affianca l’elogio del direttore sportivo Fabiani per le scelte di mercato: «Ha trasferito loro una parte del suo carattere, però smettiamola con la litania di Gattuso uguale Ringhio, solo grinta e basta. Stiamo parlando di un allenatore che fa giocare benissimo la sua squadra. Complimenti anche al direttore sportivo Fabiani, che è stato chirurgico sul mercato: ha preso quello che serviva e ha lasciato quello che non serviva».

Recent findings suggest that sabatini rifiuta l’idea che il percorso biancoceleste sia una favola: «Ma non è una favola. La Lazio è un fatto, una squadra autoritaria. Il mio augurio è che la storia della Lazio duri tutto l’anno».

Recent findings suggest that avendo lavorato come direttore sportivo per Lotito, Sabatini affronta anche il rapporto tra il presidente e i tifosi che lo contestano. Il suo giudizio parte dal riconoscimento delle qualità di Lotito: «È la magia del calcio, che restituisce quasi sempre quello che prende. Lotito è un grande presidente, lo dico con cognizione di causa. È dotato sotto il profilo temperamentale e della conoscenza calcistica».

Alla stima affianca però una critica sul coinvolgimento dei tifosi: «Sbaglia le cose facili perché sottrae a tutti, non so se involontariamente, il senso di partecipazione: i tifosi di ogni squadra si sentono i veri padroni del club, invece lui fa il presidente come gli pare, si prende tutto. Gliel’ho sempre detto ma non ha mai seguito i miei suggerimenti».

Come mai l'esclusione di Barbara Bonansea? “Sono scelte non semplici, per quello che ha rappresentato e rappresenta, ma le scelte non sono mai definitive. Io sono solito chiamare le ragazze prima della scelta, c'è stato un confronto e una spiegazione con lei. È importante, e lo sarà in futuro, ma l'ultima gara da titolare giocata è stata con noi a ottobre. La gestione di chi gioca negli Stati Uniti è particolare perché finiscono prima il campionato, e così ho scelto di portare chi sta facendo bene in campionato”.

Prima convocazione per Moraca? “La sua convocazione va nella direzione di quello che mi ha chiesto, l'ho sempre detto che non faccio le convocazioni con la carta d'identità alla mano. Ha qualità, identità di gioco e con il Como sta giocando ad alti livelli, così si è aperta questa possibilità di vestire l'Azzurro dopo che era stata attenzionata già da tempo. Io e il mio staff siamo sempre attenti a tutte le convocabili, per alcune pensiamo a un percorso nelle rappresentative giovanili, mentre per altre si aprono subito le porte della Nazionale”.

Trafford shows he has credentials to dislodge Pickford as England No 1

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford?
  • Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.
  • After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Has there been a better goalkeeper in the Premier League this season than Leeds United’s James Trafford? It is a question worth asking after his brilliance secured his side a point against Sunderland.

Opinions will vary, of course, but the body of evidence to back Trafford’s argument to permanently dislodge Jordan Pickford as England No 1 looked even stronger at the Stadium of Light.

After leaving Manchester City in the summer to play regularly following a frustrating season as backup, Trafford is proving to be a brilliant buy for Leeds. He is the most expensive British goalkeeper. More importantly, he is playing like it too.

This was a tough examination for Leeds, who were not at their best, against a typically robust and physically challenging Sunderland who are getting back to doing the things that made them so difficult to play against last season. Regis Le Bris’ side created the better chances but were repeatedly denied by Trafford.

With the windy weather playing havoc, ruining the game as a spectacle, as both sides struggled for control of the ball, the two moments of quality came from Trafford in the first half.

Goalkeeping is defined by athleticism, physical strength and reflexes, but it is also about decision-making and mental fortitude. The two saves Trafford made to deny Sunderland’s Brian Brobbey in the first half were very different, but equally impressive.

The first was deceptively hard. Although the connection on Brobbey’s shot – back in the Sunderland side and causing chaos as usual – from the edge of the area was not the cleanest and that almost made it harder, as the flight of the ball was difficult to pick up. The bounce just in front of the goalkeeper meant he had to watch it closely, judge the trajectory in the air and spin off the grass and still keep a strong hand, at full stretch, to push it away from danger.

Sources indicate that the second was, arguably, even better. Trafford had come off his line as Brobbey ran into the box. He was in a really vulnerable position, well outside his six-yard box in a one-on-one with the Netherlands international. The way he kept calm, stood up and timed when to move for the ball was superb, especially as an error could have led to a penalty.

In a recent development, trafford may have saved with his feet, but he had cramped Brobbey for room, waited for the centre forward to make a move and timed the moment to dive at his feet perfectly. It was elite-level goalkeeping in a really tricky situation that favoured the striker.

Trafford made two more fine stops in the second half too, both from Nilson Angulo. The first was getting down low to tip another bouncing ball wide, which had flicked off a defender too. The second punching another deflected effort away after a block had taken some of the venom out of the shot.

Sunderland will feel like they shaded the battle, but Robin Roefs also made two decent stops from long-range shots in the second half while substitute Sean Longstaff saw an injury-time effort cleared off the line.

Robin Roefs is at it again with another vital save for Sunderland 👏 https://t.co/SJ4qWmSHBo.

Had the former Newcastle United player scored so late in the game, the home crowd’s frustration may have boiled over. The point means Le Bris’ side have still not won a league game since August and remain bottom of the table. This is proving to be a tougher second season in the top flight for Sunderland, but if they keep playing like this, they will not remain in the bottom three for much longer.

“It’s a positive [point],” said Le Bris. “The more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.”.

“It’s a positive [point], the more positive [thing] is the way we played with intensity, togetherness - we were Sunderland today.

“It’s still a long journey, we know with this busy schedule playing in Europe, playing in the Carabao Cup, it’s a upcoming challenge for us and we need to embrace it. I think we highlighted this afternoon that we are in this challenge, we want to embrace it and be ourselves and we probably deserved a bit more today.”.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Sunderland man said: “I think the wind played a substantial part and credit to both defences and the attacks as well to be able to keep it to no goals in that swirling wind.

“I think it was a good effort from everybody so obviously we want three points from where we are in the table but keep putting up the performances like that and we’ll get some.

“As a defender it’s always nice to have a clean sheet and especially after the last few games where we haven’t had one.

Industry observers note that “It’s always something we’re looking to do and Robin [Roefs] came up with some massive saves, Omar [Alderete] coming on was really good as well and I hope my teammate’s [Nordi Mukiele] OK as well because I think that was kind of my fault. But we got the clean sheet for him so hopefully not too bad.”.

When asked about Sunderland being bottom of the league, he replied: “I think always the table reflects fairly where teams deserve to be, and I think over the course of the course of the season if we keep putting in performances like that it will represent where we should be.

“But the table always reflects where people should be but we need to keep looking at ourselves, don’t look at other anyone else, it’s no-one else’s fault but us and we know that.”.

That result means that Sunderland’s stay bottom of the Premier League and without a win in the competition since August 30, while Leeds earn their fifth draw in eight top-flight fixtures to move up to seventh on 11 points.

Industry observers note that they are doing really well, they are consistent as well. They built momentum early in the season, which is always good, so they are in a different position but anything is possible in football. We think that it is going to be a fresh opportunity to get better.

Sunderland were warned about “second season syndrome” and shrugged them off in the summer as they looked forward to their first European campaign for more than 50 years.

They had dismissed the gloomy pre-season predictions the previous year and had gone on to enjoy their most successful season in the top flight since the heady days of the Peter Reid era at the start of the century.

So when the “experts” told them it would be much harder this season—that they would no longer have the element of surprise and the squad would be badly stretched by the extra games in the Europa League—it was easy to ignore.

In a recent development, you cannot blame them. It has been a magical couple of years on Wearside where everything has gone in their favour, but reality has hit hard this season.

Sunderland are bottom of the table heading into this home game against Leeds United and have not won in the league since August.

The limp defeat at Bournemouth last weekend brought things to a head, with defender Nordi Mukiele suggesting in a post match interview that his teammates had become arrogant and had forgotten how hard they had to work last season to be successful.

There was a better performance and a decent draw away to Lech Poznan on Thursday night but Regis Le Bris’ side desperately need a win in the league.

Leeds United have been one of the story’s of the season so far and have looked dangerous in every game so far.

The return to fitness of Brian Brobbey is a big boost for Sunderland, but I don’t think any side would like to face Leeds at the moment. The home crowd will be anxious.

Régis Le Bris has made three changes to his Sunderland side.

Brian Brobbey returns to the starting line-up after recovering from a hamstring injury, while Luke O’Nien and Nilson Angulo also come into the side.

Omar Alderete and Timur Tutierov are named among the substitutes, while Kevin Danso begins a one-match suspension following his red card at Bournemouth.

Manager Daniel Farke has made three changes to his starting line-up.

Sources indicate that jaka Bijol replaces Nico Elvedi and starts alongside Tarik Muharemovic and James Justin. Brenden Aaronson and Harry Wilson both start in place of Anton Stach and Noah Okafor, supporting Dominic Calvert-Lewin in the Leeds United attack.

Leeds United: Trafford, Justin, Bijol, Muharemović, Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson, Wilson, Aaronson, Calvert-LewinSubs: Zetterer, Bard, Longstaff, Stach, Gruev, Cresswell, Nmecha, Okafor, Bahoya.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Sunderland and Leeds United at the Stadium of Light.

The final game of this gameweek sees these two Northern giants lock horns once again in a very intriguing encounter, with Sunderland especially in need of three points.

Following their opening season back in the Premier League last term, Sunderland enjoyed a historic campaign, placing seventh to qualify for European competition for the first time in 53 years. Therefore, their workload for the 2025-26 season has increased, which has caused their domestic form to suffer.

Sunderland right now find themselves bottom of the top-flight table, with just one win and four points from their opening seven league matches. They’ve lost their previous four Premier League games, but a win here could lift them out of the drop zone, depending on other results at Old Trafford and Selhurst Park.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, in the Europa League, it’s a completely different story. Regis Le Bris’ side are unbeaten, earning seven points from the first nine available. They drew 1-1 with Polish outfit Lech Poznan on Thursday evening, and given the relentless juggling act of domestic and European football, they’re already back in today against a very well-drilled team.

Recent findings suggest that leeds have made a solid start to the season and find themselves eighth in the Premier League, having only lost one match — a narrow 2-1 defeat to Arsenal at the Emirates earlier this month. Last time out, Daniel Farke’s side drew 1-1 with Manchester United at Elland Road, meaning they’re still searching for a first Premier League win since September 14.

Sources indicate that speaking in his preview, Farke stated: “To win any point in this league, you always have to be on it. And you always have to be close to be perfect, especially for normal sides - not like the top two. And for that, we are very respectful. So we don’t go into the trap and think we are bigger than we are. We are just the second year back on Premier League level. And we fight for every point.”.

Celtic accept ticket reduction for Tynecastle despite fury of fans

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.
  • The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the glitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 13:28 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 23 November 2026.

Celtic have accepted a reduced ticket allocation for their upcoming visit to Tynecastle despite calls from fans to reject the offer.

The Parkhead club, however, have stated that they will contact the Scottish Professional Football League over the glitch.

Celtic will receive 508 tickets for the Premiership encounter on November 29, which will be their first visit to Tynecastle since beating Hearts to the title in the final stages of last season, a victory which resulted in a pitch invasion from some of their fans at Celtic Park.

A Celtic statement read: 'As supporters will know, our allocation for our forthcoming match against Heart of Midlothian at Tynecastle Stadium has been cut by 20 per cent, compared to our previous visit.

'There have been a variety of views expressed to the club from supporters in relation to accepting this allocation. Some groups representing travelling supporters explained to the club that their members did not wish to accept the tickets because of the reduced allocation.

'We have taken that into consideration and also raised their concerns with the home club, who have assured us that they have spoken to Police Scotland.

Hearts had stated that only 508 tickets will be made available for Celtic fans on November 29.

'Having carefully considered all of the circumstances, we can confirm we will accept the allocation of 508 tickets.

'We respect all views and opinions on this matter, and while we are concerned and disappointed at this reduction, and others across recent years, we feel it is important that the team has the backing of our fans within the stadium for an important match.

'We realise the difficulties such a reduction can cause and in light of our discussions with supporters, we can confirm that should any supporter who is successful in the ballot, but does not wish to accept this ticket, then this will NOT affect the away ticket record moving forward.

'We thank our fans for their continued support and can confirm that we will be discussing the matter further with both the home club and the SPFL.'.

Celtic and Rangers formerly received the full Roseburn Stand for their supporters at Tynecastle, which resulted in an allocation of almost 3,500 tickets.

However, that figure was reduced to about 1,250 tickets in the 2021-22 season amid increased demand from home fans after the lockdown, and was further cut by about half.

Only Hibernian now get the full Roseburn Stand in a reciprocal agreement between the Edinburgh rivals.

Tynecastle has a capacity of about 20,000 but Hearts’ attendances are normally around 18,700 as a number of seats are not in use to create a barrier between the home and away fans.

Visiting clubs get about 800 tickets for games at Celtic Park, which has a 60,000 capacity.

  • Sources indicate that sadio Mané, capitano del Senegal che ha vinto la competizione continentale, ha affidato al suo profilo Instagram la sua soddisfazione dopo la decisione del TAS: "La decisione del Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport, che restituisce al Senegal il titolo di campione d'Africa, ci riempie di gioia.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that la Coppa d'Africa 2025 torna ufficialmente al Senegal. Il Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport ha infatti accolto il ricorso della federazione senegalese, annullando la precedente decisione della CAF che a marzo aveva attribuito il successo al Marocco con un 3-0 a tavolino.

Tutto era nato durante la finale del 18 gennaio, quando i giocatori del Senegal avevano lasciato temporaneamente il terreno di gioco in segno di protesta per un calcio di rigore assegnato agli avversari. Una volta rientrati in campo, Brahim Diaz aveva sprecato l'occasione dal dischetto e, nei tempi supplementari, Pape Gueye aveva realizzato la rete che aveva consegnato il trofeo ai Leoni della Teranga.

Sources indicate that sadio Mané, capitano del Senegal che ha vinto la competizione continentale, ha affidato al suo profilo Instagram la sua soddisfazione dopo la decisione del TAS: "La decisione del Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport, che restituisce al Senegal il titolo di campione d'Africa, ci riempie di gioia. Voglio innanzitutto ringraziare tutto il popolo senegalese, sia in patria che nella diaspora. Ci avete sostenuto dalla prima partita fino a questa decisione. La vostra fiducia ci ha dato forza nei momenti più difficili.

Grazie ai miei compagni di squadra. Conosco gli sforzi e i sacrifici che ognuno di voi ha fatto per conquistare questa seconda stella. Sono orgoglioso di aver vissuto questa avventura al vostro fianco. Grazie anche a tutto lo staff e a coloro che hanno accompagnato i Leoni.

Desidero rivolgere un messaggio di rispetto e incoraggiamento al popolo marocchino e ai giocatori del Marocco. Hanno disputato un ottimo percorso e possono esserne orgogliosi. Auguro loro il meglio per il futuro. Senegal e Marocco sono due popoli fratelli. Che la passione per il calcio continui ad avvicinarci.

It has been revealed that congratulazioni a tutti i senegalesi. Questa vittoria è anche vostra.

Visualizza questo post su Instagram Un post condiviso da Sadio Mane (@sadiomaneofficiel).

Un post condiviso da Sadio Mane (@sadiomaneofficiel).

Bruno Fernandes has been dropped for Manchester United’s crucial Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Michael Carrick has taken the decision to drop the United captain to the bench in the wake of his public criticism on Wednesday following the shambolic 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como.

Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics and has now been taken out of the starting XI.

The move had looked likely with Carrick refusing to rule out stripping Fernandes of the captaincy when quizzed on the matter on Friday.

Carrick had responded to Fernandes questioning the set up and approach by suggesting tactics can go out of the window when players are unprepared to run.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Manchester United vs Bouremouth.

United enter Sunday’s clash against Bournemouth in the grip of a deepening crisis. Wednesday night’s dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat to debutants Como extended United’s’ winless run to seven matches across all competitions - their worst sequence since 2015.

With just one victory from their opening seven Premier League fixtures, United are enduring their worst start to a top-flight season since 1986-87. Head coach Michael Carrick, a multiple champion at Old Trafford during his playing days, finds his position under severe threat, with reports suggesting another defeat could seal his departure. While both of United’s wins this season have come at home, they remain winless in their last three at Old Trafford. On an individual level, Bryan Mbeumo has offered a rare bright spark, scoring four goals in seven league outings while Bruno Fernandes continues to search for form, and the captain’s recent outburst only makes the atmosphere more febrile.

In stark contrast, Bournemouth arrive in Manchester brimming with confidence. Marco Rose’s side have enjoyed a flawless start to their inaugural European campaign, sitting joint-top of the Europa League standings after a dominant 3-0 victory over Ruben Amorim’s ten-man AC Milan on Thursday. That result marked a third consecutive home win and clean sheet, with Bournemouth outscoring opponents 8-0 in that stretch. Midfielder Marcus Tavernier has been instrumental, leading the club’s scoring charts with five goals across 11 appearances.

Bournemouth will feel no trepidation visiting Old Trafford, having gone unbeaten in their last six Premier League meetings with United (two wins, four draws). With Carrick desperate for a stabilising result and Rose’s side riding high on European momentum, today’s fixture carries significant stakes for both clubs.

Il tifo organizzato conferma la presenza il 6 dicembre e precisano che non sarà un rientro definitivo.

Così il Tifo Organizzato, tramite un comunicato pubblicato sull'account Instagram.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

A dicembre abbiamo deciso di regalarci un mese intero di Lazio.

Un anno fa questa sarebbe stata la normalità per il popolo bianco celeste ma purtroppo, un presidente tiranno e la sua pletora di tifosi giallorossi, ci hanno costretto a quell’estremo atto di amore che ci ha portato lontano da casa nostra.

In questi lunghi mesi di lontananza abbiamo capito quanto il consenso di questa protesta poggi su basi molto solide perchè ha continuato ad avere dalla sua parte un popolo che ha liberamente scelto di appoggiarla, di contro i vertici di questa società non hanno fatto assolutamente nulla per riavvicinare la tifoseria continuando ad andare nella direzione esattamente opposta ed il popolo laziale ha continuato a scegliere da che parte stare.

Poche eccezioni si sono distinte, tra tutti sicuramente ci sono mister Gattuso, che più volte ha ribadito di capire ed accettare la nostra decisione esprimendo però il “sogno” di vedere lo Stadio Olimpico pieno della sua gente, e la sua squadra (plasmata ad immagine e somiglianza del mister) che ad ogni trasferta è venuta sotto il settore ospite a prendersi il meritato applauso e sappiamo che ci sono vicini!

Per lui, per la squadra, ma soprattutto per tutti quei bambini e tifosi che hanno aderito alla protesta allontanandosi dallo stadio, a quelli che non sono riusciti ad acquistare il biglietto per il derby ed a tutti i laziali che soffrono lontano dalla propria amata Lazio, abbiamo deciso rendere omaggio entrando il 6 dicembre alla partita Lazio-Atalanta.

Caricheremo così anche i ragazzi prima della stracittadina dando un assaggio dell’ambiente che troveranno il 13 dicembre, dimostrando di essere sempre al loro fianco, perché se lo meritano!

Negli scorsi anni siamo andati ad incitarli a Formello ma ormai quel centro sportivo non lo sentiamo più “casa nostra”, sono state fatte molte amichevoli ed il signor Lotito ha pensato bene di farle a porte chiuse per paura della contestazione, ha fatto chiudere la squadra dentro un bunker fregandosene di tutti quei tifosi che avrebbero voluto vedere ed incitare quei ragazzi che oggi ci stanno regalando grandi soddisfazioni.

Non ne facciamo una questione economica, la sortita del pack scontato per tre partite non ha avuto gli effetti desiderati dall’ufficio marketing, la nostra passione non si compra con gli sconti, la nostra fede non è un prodotto da supermercato, scegliamo noi quando entrare, riprovateci ...sarete più fortunati!

Questo non vuol dire bloccare la contestazione, che per questa partita continuerà dentro lo stadio, o erroneamente pensare che si rientri definitivamente, e’ solo l’ennesima prova di unità e compattezza di un popolo contro un despota.

La protesta proseguirà con le stesse modalità di inizio anno, si continuerà a presenziare solo in trasferta ed ai derby e poi, se e quando lo vogliamo tutti noi, sceglieremo (forse) qualche altra giornata di lazialità.

Non si tratta di un passo indietro, altri lo debbono fare, ad iniziare dal tifoso romanista che occupa la sedia del responsabile della comunicazione (al derby come si comporterà!? Tiferà con cuore o continuerà a pensare al portafogli?) noi restiamo fermi sulle nostre posizioni che restano le stesse e non sono minimamente condizionate dall’ottima partenza e dalla meritata posizione in classifica.

Il nostro giudizio completamente negativo su comportamenti del signor Lotito, della gestione vergognosa ed approssimativa della prima società della Capitale, ci fanno restare fermi nella convinzione che un cambio sia urgente per stare al passo con quel mondo del calcio che viaggia ad una velocità tripla rispetto alla nostra Lazio, è doveroso nei confronti di un popolo che vive quotidianamente questo immenso amore e che invece si trova costretto a vivere in un incubo fatto di pressappochismo e botte di fortuna.

In a recent development, come già detto quando abbiamo deciso di non abbonarci e di seguire la Lazio solo in trasferta, anche questa volta chi vuole restare fuori è libero di farlo, chi invece vuole seguirci si prepari a vivere con noi 90 minuti di puro amore! Portate i bambini, mettetegli una bandiera in mano ed una sciarpa al collo e ditegli che per Natale ci regaliamo tutti un dicembre da laziali con quattro partite che ci riossigeneranno fino al derby di ritorno!

L’ex centrocampista della Lazio si allena già con il pallone e, dopo l’intervento, vuole tornare al cento per cento.

It has been revealed that matias Vecino si prepara a tornare in campo dopo l’intervento e alcuni mesi lontano dal calcio giocato. L’ex centrocampista di Lazio e Inter, che ha risolto il contratto con il Celta Vigo, racconta di stare recuperando e indica metà dicembre come il momento in cui conta di essere pronto. A Gianlucadimarzio.com ha detto: «Sto bene, sto recuperando. Mi sto preparando per il ritorno in campo».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, vecino ha ricordato le difficoltà incontrate all’inizio del percorso. Pur sapendo che l’operazione sarebbe stata abbastanza semplice, era consapevole che il recupero avrebbe richiesto tempo: «All'inizio è stato un po' più difficile, affrontare un intervento non è mai semplice. Sapevo che si trattava di un'operazione abbastanza semplice, ma che sarebbero serviti un paio di mesi per recuperare».

Sources indicate that il centrocampista è tornato a Roma con la famiglia e prosegue il lavoro insieme al suo staff. «Siamo tornati a Roma con la mia famiglia, sto facendo un bel lavoro con il mio staff. Mi sto preparando», ha spiegato. Il suo obiettivo resta riprendere a giocare, seguendo passo dopo passo il percorso di recupero.

Il classe ’91 ha indicato anche quando pensa di poter essere pronto: «Per metà dicembre sarò pronto. Sono molto ansioso di tornare, sto già lavorando sul campo con il pallone e tutto procede per il verso giusto. Poi vedremo quali opportunità potranno presentarsi».

Una volta recuperata la condizione, Vecino vorrebbe tornare in Serie A. Conosce il campionato italiano, nel quale ha giocato con Inter e Lazio, ma non intende limitare la scelta a questa possibilità. Negli ultimi mesi della scorsa stagione ha vestito la maglia del Celta Vigo.

«Sarebbe bello tornare in Serie A perché è un campionato che conosco e nel quale mi conoscono. Vedremo quello che succederà», ha dichiarato. Ha poi aggiunto: «Sono aperto anche ad altre opzioni. Dipende dalle possibilità che capiteranno».

Recent findings suggest that prima di valutare le occasioni che si presenteranno, il centrocampista vuole completare il recupero: «L'importante è stare bene, continuare a recuperare e tornare al cento per cento. Mi manca poco per raggiungere la migliore condizione, poi vedremo». La voglia di rimettersi in gioco passa dunque dal ritorno alla piena forma.

It has been revealed that gennaro Gattuso tatticamente è sottovalutato, parola di Angelo Gregucci, ex difensore della Lazio e storico collaboratore di Roberto Mancini che ha rilasciato un'intervista al Corriere della Sera (edizione Roma). "Sì. Con il Milan, una delle due partite che non ha vinto, il piano partita era perfetto. Mi sembra innovativo, tanti con lui sono migliorati. È un tecnico esigente. So che chiede molto pure a massaggiatori, fisioterapisti e altri".

In a recent development, per analizzare il percorso di crescita imperioso dei biancocelesti in campionato, trasformatosi in lotta Scudetto ormai, per la prima posizione e lo stacco su Roma e Inter. C'è un aspetto, più di altri, a sorprendere Gregucci: "La difesa", la risposta immediata. "Partiti Gila e Romagnoli, sembrava non si potesse più giocare. Al loro posto non è arrivato Paolo Maldini. Eppure la Lazio ha la miglior difesa del torneo". Con Oliver Provstgaard a catturare le luci dei riflettori, oltre che le attenzioni dell'Inter in ottica mercato, con Danilo Doekhi, Diogo Leite e Josip Sutalo il restyling totale del cuore della retroguardia ha funzionato.

In a recent development, sul ruolo di Gattuso in panchina, invece, Gregucci si è speso così: "Il merito è suo? Mi sembra evidente. Ha migliorato qualsiasi comparto: comunicazione, campo... Ha cambiato lo status delle cose. Rino non è più solo l'uomo grintoso che investe tutte le energie in ogni allenamento, arrivando a giocare con calciatori tecnicamente più forti di lui. Oggi, attraverso esperienze anche in campionati e piazze che molti avrebbero snobbato, è diventato una guida".

McInnes believes Cup final incentive will fuel Rangers in vital run of fixtures

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (913 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.

A 2-1 triumph over Motherwell on Saturday night stretched Rangers' unbeaten run to 13 matches after Ryan Naderi struck a late winner at Fir Park.

McInnes' side will host a revitalised Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, before two further home matches against Falkirk and Dundee United over the next week.

They will then face a double-header against Hibs, with a league clash at Easter Road swiftly followed by the cup final.

McInnes insists no player is guaranteed their place in the team - and challenged them to earn their place for the Hampden showpiece as they look to win the first trophy of the season.

Industry observers note that 'I think the squad looks strong at the minute,' remarked the Ibrox boss. 'We've got good options and good options from the bench to turn to.

Derek McInnes has led Rangers on a 13-game unbeaten run in all competitions.

'In this little run of fixtures, hopefully everybody will start to play a wee bit more of their part and hopefully more winning performances.

'I don't think I'll mention it [the cup final] too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team.

'Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

'We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to go away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward.

'But there's bigger games, more games like cup finals to take part in, so everybody wants to play in that one.

'I'm sure it does us no harm. I think it keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully, as I say, we're in good form.'.

Rangers are on a strong run of form and haven't lost a game since they were dumped out of Europe against Jablonec at the end of August.

The victory over Motherwell maintained their position in second in the table, four points adrift of Celtic with a game in hand.

Up against an Aberdeen side buoyed by their first win under latest boss Mario Frick at the weekend, McInnes wants his players to keep the pedal to the metal.

'I think it's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,' stated the Rangers boss.

'We've got some good fixtures at home but I think we always look at little blocks in the weeks, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, and get certain points and certain targets.

'But first thing's first now with Aberdeen. We've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game, I'll be happy.

'I think there's always a wee concern when you've got so many away on an international break, but obviously now with the January break gone, this is us working right through to March.

'When you look at those little blocks of games, and where the teams are, it's vital that we just put our shoulder to the wheel.

Industry observers note that 'Every game is going to bring up different challenges and just because we're at Ibrox, it's an advantage, but it doesn't guarantee anything. We've got to use that advantage properly.

It has been revealed that 'As I say, we've got some fixtures now ahead of the cup final. Hopefully we can get into the cup final in good form and with some strong performances.'.

Venezuelan striker Kevin Kelsy could be in line to start against Aberdeen.

Kevin Kelsy could be in line for a bigger role this week after fatigue caused by his return from international duty limited his involvement in Saturday's win over Motherwell.

The Venezuela striker was only fit enough for a substitute appearance after enduring a gruelling journey back from a friendly in Russia, with Derek McInnes admitting the travel disruption had taken its toll.

'When you go away on international duty, they go to some far-flung places and playing a friendly in Russia is not the best preparation,' stated the Rangers boss.

It has been revealed that 'There was a point on Thursday morning when we were really worried about whether he was getting back. To have ten-and-a-half hours in an airport all day Thursday isn't ideal preparation.

It has been revealed that 'He was gubbed on Friday. He was very tired when he spoke to me and told me he hadn't really slept.

'It's been a bit unusual, the preparation. We sent him home early on Friday to get a good sleep and look after himself, but we just made the call we thought was the right thing to do.

'We needed everybody at it on Saturday and we've got a significant week ahead of us where he can play his part, hopefully from the start in one or two of these games.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l’ex tecnico dell’Inter Rafa Benitez ha analizzato il momento della squadra di Chivu dopo il pareggio di Bergamo e in vista della sfida di domani sera contro lo Stoccarda.

Benitez, si può ancora sbagliare?

It has been revealed that «Sempre meno, perché ormai ne restano sempre meno di partite. Se sei in ritardo, rischi di compromettere il passaggio del turno; se sei in vantaggio, come il Como, conviene metterti in sicurezza e tentare di entrare tra le prime otto. Si può fare».

Il calendario a volte è impietoso.

According to recent reports, «La Roma a Parigi sfida non solo i campioni in carica ma anche una delle squadre più in salute. Ma c’è una domanda da porsi: cosa perderà Luis Enrique senza Kvaratskhelia e Doué? La struttura resta imponente, ci mancherebbe, ma queste sono assenze egualmente penalizzanti. E l’ultima partita di Gasperini, a Parma, ha rappresentato un segnale per chiunque: la squadra sta bene, segna e ha un centravanti pazzesco, che fa paura, come Malen. Sono argomenti anche questi».

«Si resta spiazzati dinnanzi a certe serate: avanti di due, sempre in controllo, con un attaccante come Pio Esposito che pure in Nazionale sta facendo cose enormi, subisce la reazione dell’Atalanta, che ha meriti grossi ci mancherebbe, e butta via una vittoria che pareva blindata. È un’Inter pazzerella, come suol dirsi: prima andava sotto e rimontava; ora scappa e si fa riprendere. Segna tantissimo ma subisce altrettanto e immagino che questo rappresenti il tormento di Chivu, di cui ho letto le riflessioni: riuscire a trovare l’equilibrio che manca è la sua missione, lo comprendo».

E poi c’è la catena di infortuni...

«L’Inter fa appena in tempo a ritrovare Lautaro Martinez e perde Calhanoglu. È chiaro che sono preoccupazioni anche queste, che si aggiungono a quelle del calendario. Lo Stoccarda, come qualsiasi tedesca di rango, è un’insidia e queste sono partite-trappola. Poi ci saranno la trasferta a Dortmund, mai facile, e il Liverpool a San Siro. Non è consentito rallentare, non proprio ora».

Un 4-4 come quello di Bergamo lascia scorie?

«Si fa in fretta a dimenticarlo, anzi si deve. E in questo sarà d’aiuto la personalità di Chivu. Certe fasi negative vanno risolte con le soluzioni che si trovano nello spogliatoio e con il lavoro. Diciassette reti subite in campionato rappresentano il tema dominante delle analisi dell’allenatore, che essendo stato un difensore di portata internazionale ci metterà le mani. Il primo ad avere un quadro limpido di questa Inter è lui, fidatevi».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, “Wow, wow, wow,” Harry Kane said as he took to the stage at the London Palladium after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or. Wow indeed. “I am speechless,” Kane added before launching into a heartfelt speech, the wobble in his voice showing just how much this meant to him.

In truth it would have been a travesty had the 33-year-old England captain – and Bayern Munich striker – not won with his family, friends and coaches all watching from the stalls at this famous old theatre. “All those years of sacrifice,” he remarked of his parents, Pat and Kim, his voice faltering more than ever at that moment. It was from the heart. And faltering again as he spoke about his wife and “best friend” Katie Goodland. “This is a trophy we all celebrate,” he said, talking to his children back in Bavaria. “I bring a few others [trophies] home but this one is a special one.”.

It has been revealed that kane’s speech was as outstanding as his football. “Lastly for me it is the journey,” he stated. “Learn through resilience, determination and self-belief. My journey was not easy and I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration.”.

So much for the “one-season wonder”. So much for the doubters who poured scorn on him. So much for those who believed he would never make it after loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich City and Leicester City. With varying degrees of success.

Kate Scott, the presenter, perfectly detected the emotion and noted: “You held it together. You got through it.” It highlighted how much it meant to Kane, who simply and quietly replied: “Yes”.

Recent findings suggest that what a winner. What a player. What a role model. The award given in the city where he has scored most of his goals. But he would not have been in the running for this accolade had he not been brave enough to quit Tottenham Hotspur after 19 years and move to Germany.

Kane was the favourite. But, despite its prestige, the Ballon d’Or process is an odd one. One journalist from each of the top-100-ranked Fifa countries is given a vote, with the organisers, France Football, laying out the criteria: individual performance, collective performance and fair play. In that order. They often go for the biggest name. Not the best.

Industry observers note that kane’s numbers are incredible. They speak for themselves. Those numbers show he deserved to win the prize: 65 games for club and country and 73 goals. Plus eight assists (for the judging period – August 3, 2025 to July 19, 2026). That is 61 goals for Bayern and 12 for England. That is a goal less than every 72 minutes. That is beyond elite. That is world class and legendary.

Bayern Munich and England's Ballon d'Or winner doing what he does best 🎯 https://t.co/yWNburqkpg.

For his club, that is 19 goals more than any other player in the top five European leagues. And the most since Cristiano Ronaldo scored 61 for Real Madrid in 2014-15. Kane won last season’s Golden Shoe by nine goals from Erling Haaland. He reached his century of Bundesliga goals last month in just 98 games, destroying Dieter Müller’s record set 49 years ago – he took 129 matches.

Kane became one of only two players in history (the other is Ronaldo) to score 20-plus goals across World Cups and European Championships and was the only one to score in two major club cup finals, including a hat-trick. Neither Kylian Mbappé nor Lamine Yamal, his closest rivals, scored in any finals.

In a recent development, both gave interviews declaring why they should win the Ballon d’Or. Kane? “I don’t like talking about myself,” he remarked. “The 73 goals speak for themselves.” They do.

According to recent reports, those are the facts, but there is also the football and, yes, the conduct. Kane has scored some superb goals during that period, not least for England. Take his two goals against the Democratic Republic of Congo at the World Cup that saved his team and Thomas Tuchel from an embarrassing early exit.

The Prince of Wales, who has been FA president since 2006, congratulated Kane on “a fantastic achievement”.

“A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments,” Prince William wrote on Instagram.

According to recent reports, kane, the first English player since Michael Owen in 2001 to win the award, is also the ultimate team player – so fulfilling that “collective performance” criteria – and a captain who leads by example on and off the pitch. Fair play? He was last booked in January and was cautioned just three times in 68 games and not at all in any of his 13 appearances this season.

It has been revealed that and he works hard, so very hard. Kane was in the top 10 for total distance covered at the World Cup, despite playing a game fewer than most of the others on the list. And he is often seen winning as many defensive headers in his own penalty area as attacking ones in the opposition’s.

That work extends to off the pitch, to try to maximise his ability, to do everything to be the best version of himself and to be the best. Which he has now been recognised as. And it stems from his winning mentality. Some scoffed when Kane walked into England’s press conference before the 2018 World Cup and remarked he could be top-scorer – but he proved them wrong.

Sources indicate that they probably also scoffed at the notion that he would one day be declared the best player in the world and win the Ballon d’Or. But he has done all that. It confirms England’s all-time cap holder (for now jointly with Peter Shilton) and goalscorer as one of the greats. And we are privileged to witness that greatness. Wow, what a night.

By Christian FalkGermany do not have a single player among the 30 in the running to win the Ballon d’Or in London on Monday night – but Bayern Munich do have England captain Harry Kane.

For the 35-time German champions, the award is perhaps even more notable than it is for the peerless striker himself. The Bayern hierarchy are planning to travel to the Palladium Theatre en masse to support Kane.

Recent findings suggest that kane is not only Bayern’s top striker, he is their international figurehead and, internally, their poster-boy professional. Club patron and honorary president Uli Hoeness described the England captain as the best signing in the club’s history. Hoeness even went so far as to say he loves Kane, and he is not alone in this.

Recent findings suggest that there's only one Harry Kane. https://t.co/NfZEFmjaUN.

Industry observers note that hoeness is one of many in the club’s leadership who have been endlessly promoting Kane to help the 33-year-old fulfil his lifelong dream of winning the trophy. Bayern officials have been campaigning on his behalf for weeks.

First up was manager Vincent Kompany, who remains in hospital for tests after collapsing at Bayern’s training ground on Friday. Kompany stated: “If he can now crown his career or his season with the Ballon d’Or, that would be fitting given the way he plays for the team.”.

Sources indicate that the plaudits kept coming. Whether it was sporting director Max Eberl (“He has more than earned the Ballon d’Or. Anyone who loves football loves characters like Harry Kane”), chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen (“One thing is clear – anyone talking about this year’s greatest individual honours cannot overlook Harry Kane”) or president Herbert Hainer (“Harry Kane embodies the idea that sporting greatness is incomplete without greatness of character. He would be a worthy World Footballer of the Year”), everyone at the club is fighting for Kane.

The official Ballon d’Or website has announced Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as winners of the main prize in an embarrassing blunder for the organisation.

Three separate articles were published before promptly being taken down.

The headline on Kane’s article read: ‘Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season’.

The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony takes place at the London Palladium as England and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane aims to become the first Englishman in more than 20 years to win the award. Michael Owen was the last Englishman to win the award back in 2001.

The choice of London as the host city pays tribute to the award’s inaugural winner, England’s Stanley Matthews, who won it in 1956. This also marks the first time the ceremony will be organised outside France. Kane, who scored over 70 goals for club and country in the relevant year, is among the favourites for this year’s award alongside the likes of Barcelona and Spain’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid and France’s Kylian Mbappe.

Kane won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich whereas Yamal won both La Liga and the World Cup. Yamal won the Kopa Trophy at last year’s ceremony as the best men’s young player.

In a recent development, last year’s winners were Spain and Barcelona midfielder Aitana Bonmati and France and Barcelona forward Ousmane Dembele. Dembele is aiming to become just the 11th man to win the top prize at least twice, although it would appear to be very unlikely that the Frenchman will be winning the award this evening.

Selected international journalists cast their votes based on the performances of players throughout the season. The panel consists of one representative per country from the top 100 nations in the Fifa men’s world ranking and the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Each voter ranks their top 10 candidates, with points distributed on a descending scale. They vote based on three factors: individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.

Industry observers note that in total, 13 trophies will be presented across the men’s and women’s game, including the two man Ballon d’Or awards, the best young players and best teams. The awards take into account achievements from August 3, 2025, to July 19, 2026 (August 16 for the women).

The official ceremony begins at 8pm GMT.

La Champions League torna protagonista a San Siro, dove mercoledì 25 novembre, alle ore 21, l'Inter di Cristian Chivu ospiterà lo Stoccarda nella quinta giornata della League Phase. I nerazzurri arrivano all'appuntamento dopo il rocambolesco 4-4 sul campo dell'Atalanta, una partita che ha confermato il potenziale offensivo della squadra, ma anche alcune difficoltà nella gestione delle situazioni difensive. In Europa l'Inter cerca invece la terza vittoria consecutiva, dopo i successi contro Shakhtar Donetsk e Feyenoord, per rilanciare le proprie ambizioni di qualificazione diretta agli ottavi. Riflettori puntati soprattutto sulle scelte offensive di Chivu, chiamato a gestire il rientro di Lautaro Martínez e le condizioni di Marcus Thuram, con Francesco Pio Esposito pronto a giocarsi una maglia da titolare. Tre soluzioni differenti per caratteristiche, ma tutte potenzialmente importanti contro una formazione tedesca che tende a giocare con coraggio e a lasciare spazi nelle transizioni. Sul fronte opposto, attenzione soprattutto a Deniz Undav ed Ermedin Demirović, principali riferimenti offensivi della squadra di Sebastian Hoeneß, senza dimenticare la qualità di Bilal El Khannouss sulla trequarti. Anche gli inserimenti dei centrocampisti e le situazioni da palla inattiva potrebbero offrire occasioni ai protagonisti meno attesi.

Se sei un nuovo utente per confrontare in maniera più completa le quote può essere utile analizzare anche l'eventuale bonus applicato dagli stessi operatori sui nuovi iscritti.

Tra i possibili protagonisti della notte europea di San Siro c'è Francesco Pio Esposito, pronto a ritagliarsi un ruolo importante nell'attacco dell'Inter di Cristian Chivu. Il giovane centravanti nerazzurro rappresenta una soluzione particolarmente interessante per le sue caratteristiche fisiche, la capacità di proteggere il pallone e la pericolosità all'interno dell'area di rigore. Contro uno Stoccarda che predilige un calcio propositivo e tende a lasciare spazi agli avversari, Esposito potrebbe trovare occasioni per sfruttare i rifornimenti provenienti dalle corsie esterne. Il gol di Pio Esposito viene proposto a quota 1.70 da Planetwin365, 1.82 da StarVegas, 1.85 da Eurobet e 1.94 da StarCasinò. Un confronto che evidenzia valutazioni differenti tra gli operatori, con StarCasinò che presenta la quota più alta tra quelle analizzate.

Se sei un nuovo utente per confrontare in maniera più completa le quote può essere utile analizzare anche l'eventuale bonus applicato dagli stessi operatori sui nuovi iscritti.

In a recent development, una possibilità meno scontata nel mercato dei marcatori riguarda Federico Dimarco, uno dei giocatori più importanti nello sviluppo offensivo dell'Inter. L'esterno nerazzurro rappresenta una risorsa preziosa per la qualità dei cross, la precisione sui calci piazzati e la capacità di rendersi pericoloso anche con conclusioni dalla distanza. In una partita nella quale lo Stoccarda potrebbe concedere spazi sulle corsie laterali, Dimarco potrebbe avere l'opportunità di accompagnare l'azione e cercare direttamente la porta avversaria. La sua eventuale rete rappresenta un'ipotesi meno frequente rispetto a quella di un attaccante, ma trova comunque spazio nelle valutazioni dei bookmaker. Il gol di Dimarco è quotato 3.85 da Planetwin365, 3.95 da StarVegas, 4.20 da Eurobet e 4.60 da StarCasinò. Anche in questo caso è StarCasinò a proporre la quota più elevata, con una differenza significativa rispetto agli altri operatori.

Dopo la trasferta di campionato contro l'Atalanta, l'Inter ritrova San Siro per una nuova notte europea: i nerazzurri scenderanno in campo mercoledì 25 novembre alle 21:00 contro lo Stoccarda nella gara valida per la quinta giornata della Fase Campionato della UEFA Champions League 2026/27.

Sono ancora disponibili i biglietti per assistere a Inter-Stoccarda: i tifosi possono acquistare i tagliandi su inter.it/tickets. Non solo: mercoledì 25 novembre, giorno della partita, le biglietterie nei pressi dello stadio saranno aperte a partire dalle ore 18:00.

It has been revealed that il Meazza si prepara a vivere un'altra notte europea: diverse le attività in programma per i tifosi nerazzurri. Come già accaduto prima di Inter-Club Brugge e Inter-Shakhtar, il pubblico interista è chiamato a diventare protagonista prima del calcio d'inizio della gara, partecipando in prima persona con le torce dei propri smartphone allo speciale light show organizzato dal Club. Per farlo basterà inquadrare i QR code che saranno trasmessi sui maxischermi dello stadio: tutti i tifosi interessati potranno anche partecipare cliccando su questo link.

#175660. Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (577 w)
